subject.title: Add sms.read command and SMS as a messaging channel

question: Should Android-device SMS become an OpenClaw channel, and if so should it reuse the existing `sms` channel surface or use a separate Android-node-specific boundary?
rationale: The work would grant agents read/receive/send authority over carrier SMS while overlapping the current Twilio-owned `channels.sms.*` surface, so automation cannot choose the security and product boundary safely.

options.title: Split and design first
options.body: Define a narrow Android `sms.read` command contract separately from Android-device SMS channel ingress, then implement only after sender authorization, redaction, logging, and channel naming are approved.

options.title: Limit to read command
options.body: Accept only a dangerous-by-default Android `sms.read` invoke command and defer inbound/reply channel behavior until a separate channel design is approved.

options.title: Keep SMS hosted-provider only
options.body: Leave the official `sms` channel as Twilio-backed and redirect Android-device SMS channel work unless a new plugin/API seam is explicitly sponsored.

recommendation.title: Split and design first
recommendation.body: Define a narrow Android `sms.read` command contract separately from Android-device SMS channel ingress, then implement only after sender authorization, redaction, logging, and channel naming are approved.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the current Twilio-backed `sms` channel and has the strongest current history signal for the channel/config boundary decision.
